neighbours.label: the verb 'joke' (joke/joked/joking) and 'coax'
fire: My uncle loves to joke about his terrible cooking.
At the reunion we joked about our awful school uniforms.
She was only joking when she said she would quit.
The keeper tried to coax the frightened puppy out of the crate.
Fans still joke that the stadium roof leaks every game.
He likes joking with the waiters at his favorite diner.
With a little honey you can coax the bees toward the hive.
They used to joke that the old car ran on hope.
quiet: My uncle loves to complain about his terrible cooking.
At the reunion we talked about our awful school uniforms.
She was only pretending when she said she would quit.
The keeper tried to lift the frightened puppy out of the crate.
Fans still say that the stadium roof leaks every game.
He likes chatting with the waiters at his favorite diner.
With a little honey you can attract the bees toward the hive.
They used to claim that the old car ran on hope.

notes: Peak tokens: ' joke' x6, ' coax' x6, ' joking' x4, ' joked' x2. Not probed.
